title: Tenant demotion handoff and signal sanitizer for graceful regional preemption
author: Priya Raman
description: Background & motivation: during a regional preemption event we observed abrupt tenant evictions that caused downstream KV cache loss and a spike in cold-start latency for high-priority customers. This PR introduces a coordinated 'demotion handoff' protocol that (1) soft-demotes tenants on impacted nodes, (2) conserves KV/cache state during handoff windows, and (3) sanitizes control-plane signals so transient flaps don't trigger hard evictions. Design summary: - Introduces a short-lived tenant demotion state (DEMOTED_PENDING) with an epoched handshake to the control plane. DEMOTED_PENDING signals the runtime to stop accepting new long-lived sessions while preserving KV cache and inflight prefix caches for a configurable warmup window. - Adds a SignalSanitizer middleware in the control plane that coalesces rapid health flips and applies a rate-limited reopen backoff. This reduces oscillation and prevents noisy probes from accelerating evictions. - Implements a KV conservation helper that tags critical keys with a transient retention hint enabling fast rehydration on the target node (metadata-only snapshot + async rehydrate). - Adds telemetry anchors: new metrics for demotion transitions, kv_preserve_hit/miss, sanitizer_coalesce_count, and demotion_handoff_duration. - Backoff & rollback: demotion windows are configurable by tenant weight and can be rolled back by the control plane if the region stabilizes; this PR wires an emergency rollback API for operators. Checklist: - [x] Protocol definitions and protobufs for handshake - [x] Runtime demotion state + eviction guards - [x] SignalSanitizer implementation with unit tests - [x] KV conservation metadata tagging and rehydrate path - [x] Integration test that reproduces race between health flap and preemption - [x] Telemetry and dashboard dashboards reference file - [x] Canary rollout plan in rollout notes What changed (high level): - runtime/eviction/tenant_demote.go: new demotion state machine and graceful drain paths - controlplane/signals/sanitizer.go: coalescer, rate limiter, and sanitizer rules - controlplane/handshake/handshake.proto: handshake definitions and state enums - kv/preservation/marker.go: tagging helpers + retention hint API - telemetry/metrics/demotion_metrics.yaml: metric definitions and alert rules - tests/integration/demotion_flow_test.go: end-to-end scenario reproducing race - docs/operational/tenant-demote.md: operator runbook and rollback steps Backwards compatibility & safety: default values keep behavior unchanged (demotion disabled per-tenant unless opt-in or above SLA tier). The SignalSanitizer defaults to conservative thresholds to avoid masking real failures. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated clusters first (5% traffic), monitor demotion_handoff_duration and kv_preserve_hit ratio for 24h; widen on stable signals. If adverse effects detected, rollout can be reverted via feature flag or use emergency rollback API. Testing: unit tests cover sanitizer rules, handshake state transitions, and KV tag lifecycle. Integration tests simulate flaky region heartbeats and assert no hard-eviction occurred and KV rehydrate path triggers within the warmup window. Observability: dashboards and alerting rules added; key alerts: demotion_handoff_duration > 30s (warning), kv_preserve_miss > 1% (warning), sanitizer_coalesce_count spike (info). Risk & mitigation: risk of prolonged DEMOTED_PENDING causing capacity pressure; mitigated by tenant-weighted admission and an auto-escalation to hard-evict after configurable maximum hold time. Also added a telemetry-driven auto-rollback. Notes: ties to ENG-2287 (regional preemption postmortem). This PR is intentionally conservative in defaults; further optimizations (adaptive demotion window by tenant behavior) are planned as followups.

release_notes: Introduces a conservative tenant demotion handoff protocol and a SignalSanitizer to reduce noisy preemption-induced evictions. Adds KV preservation hints for faster rehydration and anchors telemetry for monitoring. Disabled by default for standard tenants; opt-in via tenant config or enabled for high-tier SLAs.
additional_notes: Follow-ups: adaptive demotion window (ENG-2320), faster metadata snapshot path, and tenant-level opt-out by quota. Ops playbook updated in docs/operational/tenant-demote.md.
